parts:
Hi,
So, I am not a very confident coder and I am trying to update my PCA from the old plotTangentspace function to gm.prcomp but I am struggling with a few things. I can't seem to find out how to add the axes labels, change the title and correctly add the legend. I also can't seem to add my classifying factors correctly, I can only find how to add randomly group the points and I can't find out how to plot graphs of subsequent principal components. I'm sure all of this can be done with a couple functions but I can't seem to find it online.
Here is my code and attached is the graph. 

library(geomorph)
library(MASS)

mydata <- readland.tps("Flipper Ratios LM 22.TPS", specID = "ID")
coords <- as.matrix(mydata)

Flipratioslabel <- read.csv("Classifier flipper ratios.csv", header = TRUE)
is.factor(Flipratioslabel$Morphotype)

# Perform procrustes alignment and do Principal Component Analysis ---------------
flipperratios.gpa <- gpagen(mydata, print.progress = FALSE)
summary(flipperratios.gpa)
plotAllSpecimens(flipperratios.gpa$coords, mean = TRUE, links = NULL, label = TRUE, plot.param = list())

# PCA ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
flip.pca <- gm.prcomp(flipperratios.gpa$coords)
summary(flip.pca)
gps <- as.factor(c(rep("Plio.", 22), rep("Ples.", 19)))
plot(flip.pca, main = "PCA", pch = 21, cex = 1, cex.lab = 1.5, font.lab = 1, bg = gps, legend("topleft", pch = 21, pt.bg = unique(gps), legend = levels(gps)))

I hope you can help, thanks!

parts:
When you are encountering such issues, usually best to go back to basics, particularly when you are not confident with syntax. For example does the plots in this tutorial works for you as displayed?
https://learningstatisticswithr.com/book/graphics.html.

A simple trick for plotting groups as different colors would be using an as.integer() function. This works for groups less than 6 classes, since R will cycle the default colors, if you have more. If you want more control over this, you can extract as many colors as you need using palette() function, or define them.

x=rnorm(50)
gr=as.factor(c(rep('A',10),rep('B',10),rep('C',10),rep('D',10),rep('E',10)))
plot(x, col=as.integer(gr))

parts:
There is an example on the gm.prcomp help page called,  ### Advanced Plotting.  In this example, the following adjustment is made:

par(mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2))

This plot parameter adjustment makes all of the margins two lines wide, which allows scales but not labels.  If you had run this example before your others, and not reset the margins, no labels will appear no matter how much you tweak them.  To set the margins to their default values, use:

par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)

This could be the problem for missing labels.

Mike

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: plotting gm.prcomp and adding classifying factors
parts:
Laura,

 

You cannot expect R to know the order of specimens for your groups. The user must provide that. If you have a grouping variable, use that instead of inventing one as you did.

 

For labels, use the standard ‘text’ argument following plot. Below is a small example (note: I’ve shifted the labels slightly in the x,y, directions so they do not overlap the data points.

 

data(plethspecies)

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment

###  Traditional PCA

PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)

plot(PCA, main = "PCA")

text((PCA$x[,1]+0.001),(PCA$x[,2]-.002),names(Y.gpa$Csize))

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] plotting gm.prcomp and adding classifying factors
parts:
Just to follow up on Dean’s suggestion, the text function has an argument, pos, for the position of the label with respect to the points, where 1 = below, 2 = to the left, 3 = above, and 4 = to the right.  There is an argument, offset, to define the distance away from the point to add the label.  (see ?text to learn more.)  These or the way Dean demonstrated — more direct programming — give the user unlimited control over how to make their plots.  The old plotTangentSpace took this kind of control away.

Ideally plotting in R takes advantage of the base plotting system, which allows users to use any of the plotting tools available in R to manipulate plots.  The old plotTangentSpace function did not allow this, and it caused users all kinds of problems when they wanted to make quality plots for publications.  (One of the worse emails to receive was someone who had a paper accepted but had to come up with a better quality plot when they submitted a plotTangentSpace plot as a figure…)  With any geomorph plot, you should be able to change the points, change colors, add text, add points, add arrows, etc., and use bmp, tiff, jpeg, pdf, or png functions to save high-resolution copies of plots.  

One “bonus” the old plotTangentSpace function had was that it absolved users from essential plotting skills in R, which is historically unfortunate.  If data analysis in R is preferred, then acquiring some plotting skill in R should also be a goal.  Some people prefer advanced plotting with ggplot2 and geomorph plots should be quite amenable to using ggplot2.  In Dean’s example, if it were changed to this:

pca.plot <- plot(PCA, main = "PCA”)

then pca.plot$plot.args would have the plotting parameters one might wish to use and change in a ggplot approach.

Finally, I do not understand the issue with coloring groups.  I tried Dean’s example,

> data(plethspecies)
> Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment
> ###  Traditional PCA
> PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)
>

> spec.names <- names(Y.gpa$Csize)
> spec.names
[1] "P_cinereus"       "P_electromorphus" "P_hoffmani"       "P_hubrichti"     
[5] "P_nettingi"       "P_richmondi"      "P_serratus"       "P_shenandoah"    
[9] "P_virginia"      
> 
> my.colors <- rep(1, length(spec.names))
> my.colors[spec.names %in% c("P_cinereus", "P_shenandoah" )] <- 2
> my.colors
[1] 2 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 1
> 
> pca.plot <- plot(PCA, main = "PCA", pch = 21, bg = my.colors)
> text(PCA$x[,1:2], spec.names, pos = 3, offset = 0.5)

and got this plot


then I changed the colors to a factor; i.e., 

> pca.plot <- plot(PCA, main = "PCA", pch = 21, bg = as.factor(my.colors))
> text(PCA$x[,1:2], spec.names, pos = 3, offset = 0.5)

And I got the same plot.  R should be able to convert factors to numeric values for plot colors, so I am not sure what the issue is.

Best,
Mike
